guidelines.detail: refines EVT-03 (The description supports waiting for the product’s arrival and making the penalty conditional on a wait exceeding ten days. The generated catch event reflects the event-based wait, whereas the reference’s service task does not follow BPMN event semantics. EVT-03 already covers catch events for waits; this guideline adds the elapsed-time decision and conditional action. It does not copy the referen)

same as LRN-085 (The description makes the penalty depend on whether arrival takes more than a stated duration. The records show the reference uses a service task for waiting and a gateway for the elapsed-time decision, while the generated model uses catching events and an event-based gateway. This supports modeling the wait as an event and explicitly evaluating the elapsed-time condition; the learned guideline LR)

The description confirms a wait for an occurrence and a subsequent elapsed-time decision, but M1 identifies the reference element as a service task for waiting. A wait for an occurrence should be modeled as an intermediate catch event, not a task, so the reference’s expected element choice conflicts with BPMN semantics. I therefore cannot derive a guideline from this reference difference.

documentation rule EVT-03 not applied (The description places an arrival between the reorder and subsequent work, while the generated model uses an intermediate catch event and the reference uses a task. The documented guideline EVT-03 already says to use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger, so this guideline is already covered.)

documentation rule EVT-03 not applied (The description implies waiting for the product to arrive before continuing, while the generated model has no counterpart for that wait (M1). Modeling the occurrence as a catch event follows the documented guideline EVT-03, so this is not a new guideline.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says the process must wait for an occurrence and makes a subsequent action depend on whether the wait exceeded a stated duration: Model the wait for the occurrence with an intermediate catch event, then use an exclusive gateway to evaluate the elapsed-time condition and route the qualifying branch to the action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says the process must wait for an occurrence and makes a subsequent action depend on whether the wait exceeded a stated duration

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that the process waits for a stated time or period to end before continuing: Model the wait as an intermediate catch timer event, then connect it to the subsequent activity rather than representing the passage of time as a task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that subsequent work depends on an expected external object becoming available

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use an intermediate catch event when flow waits for a trigger and an intermediate throw event when flow emits or raises a result.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an external occurrence or item is expected after an action and the process continues after it occurs
